lessons.title: Capstone: a sustained conversation about work, study and plans
lessons.explanation: This lesson assembles the level into a conversation held across several turns, which is a different skill from producing any single well-formed utterance. Conversation analysis gives the structure. A conversation is viewed as a collection of turns of speaking in which errors or misunderstandings are addressed with repairs and turns are marked by delay and other linguistic features; its basic structures include turn-taking organization, recipient design, sequence organization with adjacency pairs such as question-answer and offer-acceptance or refusal, and repair. Turn-taking itself is the organisation in which participants speak one at a time in alternating turns, with processes for constructing contributions, responding to previous comments and transitioning to a different speaker. The practical consequences of that analysis are concrete. First, a turn is designed for its recipient: the same content addressed to a friend and to a director is built differently, which in Russian means a decision between ты and вы that you make once and then hold. Second, adjacency pairs create expectations, so a question obliges an answer and an offer obliges an acceptance or a refusal; leaving the second part missing is itself a move. Third, repair is a normal part of conversation rather than a failure, and Russian has a short standard repertoire: Извините, я не расслышала (eez-vee-NEE-tye, ya nye ras-SLY-sha-la) - sorry, I did not catch that; Повторите, пожалуйста (pav-ta-REE-tye, pa-ZHA-loos-ta) - please repeat; Что вы имеете в виду? (shto vy ee-MYE-ye-tye v vee-DOO) - what do you mean?; Вы имеете в виду, что...? - do you mean that...?. Repair costs one turn and saves a conversation, and using it is a sign of competence rather than weakness. For plans, the grammar you need is already assembled from earlier lessons and only has to be kept straight. Собираться plus the infinitive gives an intention: Я собираюсь поехать к родителям (ya sa-bee-RA-yus pa-YE-khat k ra-DEE-tye-lyam) - I am planning to go to my parents. Буду plus an imperfective infinitive gives a future activity: Я буду готовиться к экзамену (ya BOO-du ga-TO-veet-sya k ek-za-MYE-noo) - I will be preparing for the exam. The perfective non-past gives a single planned completion: Я сдам экзамен в июне (ya ZDAM ek-za-MYEN v ee-YOO-nye) - I will have taken the exam in June. For joint proposals Cornell gives the construction and its constraint in one line: use давай(те) plus an infinitive to express let us with imperfective verbs, and давай(те) plus the non-past to express let us with perfective verbs, the whole construction being a future expression. So Давайте говорить по-русски (dav-VAY-tye ga-va-REET pa-ROOS-kee) - let us speak Russian - is correct with the imperfective infinitive, and Давайте поговорим о работе (dav-VAY-tye pa-ga-va-REEM a ra-BO-tye) - let us have a talk about work - is correct with the perfective non-past, while mixed forms are not Russian. The vocabulary of the topic area is worth fixing before the conversation rather than during it: собеседование (sa-bee-SYE-da-va-nee-ye, a job interview), повышение (pa-vy-SHE-nee-ye, a promotion), стажировка (sta-zhee-ROF-ka, an internship), подрабатывать (pad-ra-BA-ty-vat, to work part-time), поступить в университет (pa-stoo-PEET v oo-nee-veer-see-TYET, to enrol at university), диплом (dee-PLOM, a diploma or degree), планы на будущее (PLA-ny na BOO-doo-shchee-ye, plans for the future) and отпуск (OT-poosk, leave, holiday). The final skill in a sustained conversation is holding the thread: coming back to an earlier point with кстати (by the way) or with насчёт того, что вы сказали (na-SHCHOT ta-VO, shta vy ska-ZA-lee, about what you said), and closing with Договорились (da-ga-va-REE-lees, agreed, that is settled). Four conversational items belong in the same list: собеседник (sa-bee-SYED-neek) is the person you are talking with, поддержать разговор (pad-dyer-ZHAT raz-ga-VOR) is to keep a conversation going, переспросить (pee-ree-spra-SEET) is to ask again, and уточнить (oo-tach-NEET) is to clarify.
lessons.example: Here is a five-turn conversation about work, study and plans, with the turn-management move labelled in each turn. - Кем вы работаете? (kyem vy ra-BO-ta-ye-tye) - What do you do? [turn-opening question; sets an adjacency pair and fixes the register as вы] - Я работаю в отделе логистики, но сейчас учусь на курсах. Я собираюсь поступить в университет в следующем году. (ya ra-BO-ta-yoo v at-DYE-lye la-GEES-tee-kee, no see-CHAS oo-CHOOS na KOOR-sakh. ya sa-bee-RA-yus pa-stoo-PEET v oo-nee-veer-see-TYET v SLYE-doo-yoo-shchem ga-DOO.) [answer, then a volunteered plan; собираться plus a perfective infinitive for an intention] - А что вы хотите изучать? (a shto vy kha-TEE-tye ee-zoo-CHAAT) [a follow-up question that takes up the previous turn rather than changing topic] - Мне кажется, экономику. Но, честно говоря, я не совсем уверена: работа занимает много времени. Должно быть, будет трудно совмещать. (mnye KA-zhet-sya, e-ka-NO-mee-koo. no, CHEST-na ga-va-RYA, ya nye saf-SYEM oo-VYE-rye-na: ra-BO-ta za-nee-MA-yet MNO-ga VRYE-me-nee. dolzh-NO byt, BOO-det TROOD-na sav-mye-SHCHAT.) [opinion frame, then an explicit marker of uncertainty, then a hedged deduction with должно быть] - А если учиться на заочном? Тогда можно работать. (a YES-lee oo-CHEET-sya na za-OCH-nam? tag-DA MOZH-na ra-BO-tat) [an offer framed as a conditional question, which is softer than a direct proposal] - Это интересная мысль. Но, по-моему, на заочном меньше практики. Давайте вернёмся к этому позже - сейчас мне нужно сдать экзамен на курсах. (EH-ta een-tee-RYES-na-ya mysl. no, pa-MO-ye-moo, na za-OCH-nam MYEN-she PRAK-tee-kee. dav-VAY-tye veer-NYOM-sya k EH-ta-moo PO-zhe - see-CHAS mnye NOOZH-na zdat ek-za-MYEN na KOOR-sakh.) [acknowledgement of the offer, a hedged disagreement with по-моему, a proposal with давайте plus the perfective non-past вернёмся, and a deferral with a concrete reason] Now examine the conversational machinery turn by turn. The first turn establishes вы and creates an expectation that only an answer can satisfy. The second turn satisfies it and then extends it, which is what makes a conversation grow rather than tick over, and the speaker has paired собираться with a perfective infinitive, which is the correct pairing for an intention. The third turn is a follow-up question that reuses the previous speaker's material, and this is the single most reliable way to make a conversation sound like conversation rather than an interrogation. The fourth turn contains the level's most advanced move: an opinion frame, an explicit marker of uncertainty and a modal deduction, all in three sentences, with the deduction hedged by должно быть rather than asserted. The fifth turn repairs a potential conflict: the offer of evening study is acknowledged before it is qualified, the disagreement is hedged with по-моему and меньше практики rather than declared wrong, the proposal uses the correct давайте plus perfective non-past, and the deferral is given a concrete reason. Note that the conversation never descends to yes-or-no: every turn adds information the previous turn did not contain, and the one potential face-threat is wrapped in an acknowledgement. Note also what the speakers do not do: nobody switches from вы to ты, nobody interrupts, and nobody answers a question with a single word.
lessons.question: In the conversation above, the speaker wants to propose that the two of them continue the discussion another time. Which form is correct, and why?
lessons.answer: Давайте вернёмся к этому позже - let us come back to this later - because Cornell states that давай(те) takes the imperfective infinitive with imperfective verbs and the perfective non-past with perfective verbs, and вернёмся is the perfective non-past.
lessons.distractor: Давайте вернуться к этому позже - because давайте is always followed by the infinitive, whatever the aspect of the verb.
lessons.correction: The distractor is the natural over-generalisation, and it is wrong for perfective verbs. Cornell's rule is a pairing rather than a single pattern: use давай(те) plus the infinitive with imperfective verbs, as in Давайте читать, and давай(те) plus the non-past with perfective verbs, as in Давайте прочитаем. The infinitive after давайте is therefore an imperfective infinitive, not any infinitive. Cornell also notes that the construction is a future expression and that with some perfective verbs of motion the давайте may be dropped altogether, as in Пойдём в кино, which is why Пойдём sounds natural and slightly more informal than Давайте пойдём.

depth.definitions: Turn: a stretch of talk by one speaker bounded by another speaker's talk. Turn-taking: the organisation by which participants speak one at a time in alternating turns. Adjacency pair: two linked turns of complementary types, such as question-answer, offer-acceptance or offer-refusal and compliment-response, divided into first pair parts and second pair parts. Recipient design: the shaping of a turn for the particular person being addressed. Repair: the conversational machinery for addressing errors or misunderstandings. Давайте construction: давай(те) plus an imperfective infinitive, or plus a perfective non-past, as a future expression for joint proposals. Заочное обучение: part-time or distance study, contrasted with очное, full-time study. Prerequisite: the whole level - argument reading from lesson 81, register from lesson 82, subjectless and passive sentences from lesson 83, verbal nouns from lesson 84, aspect in procedure from lesson 85, evidentiality and hedging from lesson 86, politeness from lesson 87, procedure production from lesson 88 and summarising from lesson 89.
depth.mechanism: A sustained conversation is built out of three mechanisms, and each has a failure mode you can diagnose. The first is sequential: every turn is heard as a response to the previous one, so adjacent turns must be type-matched, and a second pair part that ignores the first is heard as evasion rather than as a change of subject. This is why a follow-up question is more conversationally competent than an unrelated new one: it accepts the obligation the previous turn created and then adds to it. The second mechanism is recipient design, and in Russian it is largely a matter of the ты and вы decision plus the associated forms of imperatives. The choice is made by the speaker who has the greater claim to deference, and changing it mid-conversation is itself a move with meaning, which is why the polite course is to hold the form you began with until the other person proposes otherwise. The third mechanism is repair, which handles the fact that speech is produced in real time and is therefore full of partial utterances, self-corrections and mishearings. Russian repair is highly conventionalised: Извините plus a statement of what went wrong, Повторите, пожалуйста, and the checking formulas Что вы имеете в виду? and Вы имеете в виду, что...?. The limits deserve care. Conversation analysis describes structure; it does not license performing a list of moves mechanically, and a speaker who manufactures an adjacency pair for every sentence sounds like a textbook. Real Russian conversation also tolerates overlap and long monologues in some settings, particularly among friends and in professional briefings, so the alternating-turn norm is a default rather than a law. And the transcription of actual conversation is a research method with its own conventions, so reading conversation analysis is not the same as listening to Russian: recordings and live practice remain necessary.
depth.secondExample: Take the same conversation into the written register as an email, and watch which conversational machinery survives. Здравствуйте, Светлана Сергеевна! Спасибо за разговор вчера. Как я поняла, вы советуете сначала сдать экзамен на курсах, а потом решать насчёт университета. Я согласна с этим. Что касается заочного обучения, я подумаю: мне кажется, мне нужна практика, но не хочу ошибиться. Напишите, пожалуйста, когда вам удобно продолжить разговор. С уважением, Мария (ZDRAST-vooy-tye, svyet-LA-na sye-RGYE-yev-na. spa-SEE-ba za raz-ga-VOR FCHEE-ra. kak ya pa-NYA-la, vy sa-VYE-too-ye-tye sna-CHA-la zdat ek-za-MYEN na KOOR-sakh, a pa-TOM ree-SHAT na-SHCHOT oo-nee-veer-see-TYE-ta. ya sag-LAS-na s EH-teem. shto ka-sa-YET-sya za-OCH-na-va a-boo-CHE-nee-ya, ya pa-DOO-ma-yoo: mnye KA-zhet-sya, mnye noozh-NA PRAK-tee-ka, no nye ha-CHOO a-shee-BEET-sya. na-pee-SHEE-tye, pa-ZHA-loos-ta, kag-DA vam oo-DOB-na pra-dal-ZHEET raz-ga-VOR. s oo-va-ZHE-nee-em, ma-REE-ya.) Several things have changed. The turn structure has become paragraph structure, and the adjacency pairs have become explicit: a request for a reply replaces the conversational expectation of one. The repair apparatus has vanished, because writing can be revised, and in its place come the resumptive formulas Как я поняла (as I understood) and Что касается (as for). The hedging has become more formal rather than weaker: мне кажется remains, but the conversational должно быть has given way to a stated plan to think it over, я подумаю. And the politeness has moved from turn design to address form and closing formula, with the patronymic greeting and С уважением. What survives is the substance: the agreement, the reservation and the request to continue. This is the same person talking to the same person about the same decision, and the transformation is the register flip from lesson 82 applied to an entire exchange.
depth.mistake: The first error is monologue. A learner who prepares a rich answer and delivers eight sentences about their work has satisfied the question and killed the conversation, because no adjacency pair was created for the other person. The repair is to end contributions with a question or an invitation, and to answer the previous turn before adding anything new. The second error is answering in minimum units. Да, работаю answers the letter of Кем вы работаете? and gives the other speaker nothing to build on; Russian conversation expects the answer plus one piece of volunteered material. The third error is the unilateral ты. Switching from вы to ты is a move the other person effectively controls in most situations, and a learner who switches because the conversation has become friendly sounds presumptuous or unreflective; wait for an invitation such as Давайте на ты or a change in how they address you. The fourth error is refusing to repair: a learner who does not understand and says nothing accumulates a conversation built on a mishearing, and Russian speakers generally prefer Повторите, пожалуйста to silence. The fifth is the grammatical trap of this lesson, using an infinitive after давайте with a perfective verb, as in Давайте поехать instead of Давайте поедем; the pairing is an imperfective infinitive or a perfective non-past, and the mixed form is not Russian.
depth.application: Task: hold a four-minute conversation with a partner - or, if no partner is available, record both sides yourself, alternating turns with no gaps - on the prompt Чем вы занимаетесь и что вы собираетесь делать в следующем году? Your four turns must each contain one of the level's structures: an intention with собираться, a hedged opinion, a deduction or an uncertainty marker, and a proposal with давайте. Then listen to the recording and score it. Model response, one turn: Я работаю в школе и учусь на курсах. В следующем году я собираюсь поступить в университет на исторический факультет. Я не совсем уверена, что смогу совмещать, но, по-моему, стоит попробовать. Давайте обсудим это подробнее - как вы думаете, реально ли это? Self-review rubric: (1) did every one of your turns respond to the previous turn before adding something new? (2) did you use all four required structures correctly - собираться with a perfective infinitive, a hedged opinion frame, an uncertainty or deduction marker, and давайте with a perfective non-past? (3) did you hold the address form constant, and did you produce at least one repair or checking question during the conversation? Three yes answers passes; then repeat with the register flipped to вы if you used ты, or the reverse if you used вы, and note how much of your vocabulary has to change.
depth.summary: A sustained conversation is an alternating sequence of recipient-designed turns in which adjacency pairs create obligations, repair keeps the exchange accurate, and the speaker adjusts register, hedging and proposal forms to the person being addressed. The level's apparatus has been assembled for exactly this: reading an argument in lesson 81, placing it in a register in 82, parsing subjectless and compressed sentences in 83 and 84, controlling aspect in 85, marking evidence and confidence in 86, softening disagreement in 87, producing a procedure in 88 and summarising in 89. Two limits should be kept in view. Conversational structure is a description rather than a script, so mechanical turn-taking sounds artificial; and reading conversation analysis is not listening practice, which remains necessary. What no lesson quiz can establish is that you can hold such a conversation with a Russian speaker: that is a performance claim and it needs a real interlocutor, so arranging one is the next task.

visual.title: Five-turn conversation scaffold with the move and the Russian frame for each turn
visual.description: A labelled scaffold of five ordered turns for a conversation about work, study and plans, each naming the conversational move, the Russian structure and the failure it prevents. Text steps, not video.
steps: Turn 1 - Open a topic with a question. Structure: a question in the вы or ты form, which fixes the address form for the whole exchange. Example: Чем вы занимаетесь? Failure prevented: an exchange with no first pair part, which leaves the other speaker nothing to answer.

Turn 2 - Answer, then volunteer one extension. Structure: a plain answer plus собираться with a perfective infinitive for an intention. Example: Я работаю в школе и собираюсь поступить в университет. Failure prevented: the minimum answer, which satisfies the question and stops the conversation.

Turn 3 - Take up the other speaker's material. Structure: a follow-up question built from their words, with кстати if you are returning to an earlier point. Example: А что вы хотите изучать? Failure prevented: serial unrelated questions, which read as an interrogation.

Turn 4 - Contribute a hedged opinion and a marked uncertainty. Structure: по-моему or мне кажется plus не совсем уверена, and a deduction with должно быть if you are inferring. Example: По-моему, это реально, но я не совсем уверена. Failure prevented: flat assertion, which forecloses the other speaker's contribution.

Turn 5 - Propose, agree or defer, and repair if needed. Structure: давайте with an imperfective infinitive or a perfective non-past; Договорились to close; Повторите, пожалуйста or Что вы имеете в виду? to repair. Example: Давайте вернёмся к этому позже. Failure prevented: an exchange that ends without a next step, or one left running on a mishearing.

questions.prompt: A colleague writes Должно быть, он уже ушёл. How should you read the modal?
questions.answer: As a confident deduction: должно быть is invariable and marks the speaker's inference about a past event.
questions.distractor: As an obligation: должно agrees with the subject and means he was obliged to leave.
questions.correction: The two forms differ by one letter and by their whole grammatical behaviour. Должен, должна, должны agree with a subject and mean obligation; должно быть is invariable and marks a deduction from indirect evidence. Reading the second as the first will systematically mistranslate Russian reports, where deduction with a weakening of obligation is the common case.

questions.prompt: In a meeting you must reject a colleague's proposal, and you will work with this person for years. Which Russian move best fits the politeness logic of conceding before objecting?
questions.answer: Я понимаю вашу точку зрения, но я не совсем согласен с этим предложением - concede the standing, then hedge the objection.
questions.distractor: Это предложение нельзя принять, потому что оно не работает - remove the person from the sentence so nobody is accused.
questions.correction: The impersonal verdict looks neutral but closes the topic while still coming from you, so it damages the colleague's room to respond. A hedge such as я не совсем согласен presents the objection as a degree of the speaker's view, which is a claim the other person can argue with, and the concessive opener protects face before the objection lands. Impersonal constructions are not rude in themselves - they belong in reports, as lesson 83 showed - but they are the wrong instrument between two people negotiating a decision.

questions.prompt: You must explain a four-step process aloud to a group of visitors you have just met. Which opening instruction is correct, and why?
questions.answer: Возьмите карту и посмотрите на схему, with -те on both verbs, because -те is the default for a group and for a stranger.
questions.distractor: Надо взять карту и посмотреть на схему, because impersonal frames are the neutral choice when the audience is unfamiliar.
questions.correction: Impersonal frames belong to the written manual register, not to a live demonstration where you are standing in front of people who must act. For a group or a single stranger the addressed -те imperative is the default, and it is also the shorter and clearer option in speech. Note that возьмите needs memorising: брать gives возьми rather than a form derivable from the non-past stem alone.

questions.prompt: After your oral summary, a listener asks whether a particular claim was the text's or yours. What is the correct repair?
questions.answer: Attach a frame to the claim: По мнению авторов отчёта... - attribution rather than confidence is what is missing.
questions.distractor: Add a hedge: Наверное... - lowering your confidence removes the ambiguity about ownership.
questions.correction: A hedge marks how sure the speaker is; it does not say whose claim is being reported, so the ambiguity survives and the claim is additionally weakened. The repair is an attribution frame - по мнению, по данным, согласно, or a reporting verb with a что-clause - which moves the claim back to its source. This is the same equipment as lesson 76's reported speech and lesson 86's evidentiality, and its absence does the most damage in a summary, where the listener has no source text to check you against.

questions.prompt: A conversation about work and study has stalled: your last three answers were Да, Нет and Не знаю. Which single change restores it?
questions.answer: Answer the question and then add one piece of volunteered information plus a follow-up question of your own.
questions.distractor: Introduce a completely new topic so that the conversation does not run out of material.
questions.correction: Minimum answers satisfy the adjacency pair and give the other speaker nothing to build on, and an unrelated new topic abandons the obligation the previous turn created, which reads as evasion. Conversation analysis treats each turn as hearably a response to the one before it, so the competent move is to answer, extend, and hand the turn back with a question. Volunteering material is what makes a learner's conversation grow rather than tick over.

questions.prompt: A report opens with В связи с увеличением числа заказов было принято решение о проверке оборудования. Which decomposition of this sentence is defensible from its grammar alone?
questions.answer: It reports a decision as an event with no agent named, through one verbal noun and one short passive participle, while the increase is stated as a fact inside a prepositional phrase.
questions.distractor: Its subject is увеличение, which performed the decision, and проверка is the object the increase acted upon.
questions.correction: There is no nominative subject: было принято is a neuter singular short passive participle agreeing with решение, and it implies no agent, unlike a third-plural form such as решили. Увеличение sits inside the frame в связи с plus the instrumental, so it is a circumstance rather than a doer. Разбор of this kind is what lesson 82's register work and lesson 84's verbal-noun tests are for; the sentence is dense, not agentive.

questions.prompt: Which spoken-register sentence is the correct expansion of После проверки документов мы подписали договор?
questions.answer: Когда мы проверили документы, мы подписали договор - the verbal noun becomes a finite perfective verb in a time clause.
questions.distractor: После того как документы проверены, мы подписали договор - keep the short participle so the check stays impersonal.
questions.correction: Both parts of the distractor's clause are grammatical, but the result is still a written-register sentence, because a short passive participle in a time clause is bookish rather than conversational. The expansion that serves speech supplies a subject, a tense and an aspect: мы проверили, perfective, one completed act by two named people. The exercise is the register flip in the written-to-spoken direction, and the test of success is whether every word of the result is sayable aloud without sounding like a form being read.

questions.prompt: A procedure reads Не открывайте крышку and, three steps later, Откройте крышку через пять минут. Why do the two imperatives differ in aspect?
questions.answer: The prohibition is a standing ban and takes the imperfective, while the later step is one bounded completion and takes the perfective.
questions.distractor: The prohibition is polite and the later step is a strict order, and aspect carries the politeness.
questions.correction: Cornell's politeness effect exists, but it is not doing the work here, because a lid instruction is not a host-and-guest cliché. Aspect separates a standing ban that denies every occurrence of the action from a single bounded act to be completed once. The imperfective under negation is the natural negative of instruction, exactly as in narrative negation, and mixing the two readings will turn a safety prohibition into a vague suggestion.

questions.prompt: An analysis piece states Маловероятно, что проект завершат в этом году. What is the writer committed to?
questions.answer: A judgement that completion within the year is unlikely, with the possibility left open and the completion assigned to unnamed people.
questions.distractor: An assertion that the project will not be completed this year, with the third-plural form naming the responsible party.
questions.correction: Маловероятно is a low rung on the likelihood scale, not a denial; for a denial Russian would use не завершат or a construction with невозможно. Завершат is a third-plural perfective non-past, so it implies unnamed human agents will do the completing, but implication of agency is a separate matter from the strength of the writer's commitment. Reading both scales at once - evidence and confidence - is the skill lesson 86 built.

questions.prompt: You have to disagree with a director in a written report and you want the objection to survive scrutiny. Which combination is best?
questions.answer: Keep the evidence attribution and soften only your own stance: По данным отчёта, этот вывод кажется преждевременным.
questions.distractor: State the objection impersonally and without attribution so that it reads as an objective finding: Этот вывод преждевременен.
questions.correction: Dropping the attribution is the fatal move: your objection then looks like a finding of the report rather than your reading of it, and it cannot be revised without loss of face if you turn out to be wrong. Keeping по данным отчёта preserves the source's role, and кажется marks the stance as yours. Formality is not politeness, but in written evaluation the hedge and the attribution perform the same repair that a concessive opener performs in speech.

questions.prompt: You record a four-sentence oral summary and find that most of its phrases also occur in the source. What is the diagnosis and the remedy?
questions.answer: You have recited rather than paraphrased; the remedy is to re-lexicalise the claim, the support and the conclusion in your own words, keeping the attributions.
questions.distractor: You have compressed too aggressively; the remedy is to add more of the source's detail back in.
questions.correction: A paraphrase is defined as a rewording that retains the meaning, so shared phrasing is a definitional failure rather than a matter of style, and adding detail makes the recitation longer rather than better. The remedy is to rebuild each part with different words, which is also what forces you to parse the content. What must not be replaced is the set of attributions and hedges, because those carry the source's commitment rather than its wording.

questions.prompt: Halfway through a conversation that began with вы, the other speaker starts using ты and your first name. What is the appropriate response?
questions.answer: Follow their lead and shift to ты, because the invitation is theirs to give and you are responding to it.
questions.distractor: Apologise for having used вы and restart the conversation in the informal register to correct the mistake.
questions.correction: The вы to ты shift is controlled in most Russian situations by the speaker with the greater claim to deference, and a learner who follows an explicit invitation is behaving correctly. Apologising invents an error that did not occur and draws attention to the register rather than to the content. What matters is to make the shift once and then hold it consistently, since drifting back and forth reads as uncertainty about the relationship itself.

questions.prompt: Read two sentences together: Говорят, что завод закрывают. Вряд ли это правда. What does the second sentence do?
questions.answer: It adds the speaker's own low-confidence judgement of the reported claim, without denying that the report exists or that people said it.
questions.distractor: It denies the implication of human agency that the third-plural form carried in the first sentence.
questions.correction: The second sentence evaluates the proposition, not the report's existence: говорили remains true even if the claim is false, which is why reported speech needs a frame rather than a fact-check. The third-plural form in говорят does imply human sources, but вряд ли addresses the content rather than the agency. Keeping these two layers apart - what was said, and what the current speaker thinks of it - is what lets you read Russian commentary without mistaking a quote for an opinion.

questions.prompt: Compare a news item that says точную стоимость работ не сообщили with a report that says точная стоимость работ не сообщена. What is the essential difference?
questions.answer: The third-plural form implies unnamed people who failed to report the figure, while the short participle states the condition of the information and names nobody.
questions.distractor: The short participle is weaker because participles can only describe states, so it cannot refer to a failure at all.
questions.correction: Both sentences refer to the same missing information, and the difference is agency rather than strength. Cornell's test applies exactly here: the third plural licenses an unnamed human actor, and the short participle does not. Short participles do commonly describe states - Магазин закрыт - but they also carry event readings with an auxiliary, as in Статья была написана, so the limitation in the distractor is not a rule. Choosing between the two constructions is an editorial decision about whom the reader will hold responsible.

questions.prompt: You must summarise a written recipe aloud to a friend who is cooking now. What must change, and what must not?
questions.answer: The impersonal and -ся frames become addressed imperatives, while the aspect pattern of each step is preserved.
questions.distractor: The aspect pattern must be inverted, because speech prefers the perfective where writing prefers the imperfective.
questions.correction: The register flip changes who performs the steps and therefore whether the text addresses a person; it does not change what each step means. If a written step is iterative, as in помешивайте, the spoken step stays iterative, and if it is a bounded completion the spoken step stays perfective. Inverting the aspect pattern would silently change the cooking instructions, turning a keep-stirring step into a stir-once step, which is the kind of error that makes a summary dangerous rather than merely inelegant.

questions.prompt: While summarising a written report aloud you find it convenient to keep the report's verbal nouns and participles because they are shorter. What is the cost?
questions.answer: You lose the report's attributions and hedges if you drop them, and you keep a written register in speech; the compressed forms are not themselves the content.
questions.distractor: No cost: deverbal nouns and participles preserve the report's exact meaning, so keeping them is the most accurate way to summarise.
questions.correction: The compressed forms are a register device, not a content device: they carry no person and no tense, so they under-specify exactly what a spoken summary has to supply. What matters for accuracy is not the morphological shape but the preserved commitment - по мнению, по данным, по-видимому, маловероятно - because those are what tell the listener how far the report went. A summary in full written register also violates the requirement to speak in your own words, which lesson 89 established as part of the definition.

questions.prompt: A long article asserts a claim that its own cited authors hold; you disagree with it and want to say so in a conversation. Which sequence is best?
questions.answer: Report the claim with its attribution, state your own view with an opinion frame, concede the part you accept, and only then hedge the objection.
questions.distractor: State your verdict first so the listener knows where you stand, then explain what the article said.
questions.correction: Leading with a verdict gets the disagreement on the record before anyone knows what is being disagreed with, which is the blunt pattern the politeness material warns against and which also risks disagreeing with the wrong party - the cited authors rather than the writer. The sequence works because it separates three things in order: what the source said and whose claim it is, what you think, and where the disagreement actually falls. The concession is not decoration; it is what keeps the other person able to answer.
